records.name: Nebinger PTA
records.summary: Parents, teachers and neighbors who support George W. Nebinger School. They plan school events, fundraisers and volunteer days, and anyone can come to the general meetings.
records.what_you_do: Come to a general meeting, sign up for a volunteer shift on the school's volunteer calendar, or help plan events. Members also help with teacher appreciation, fundraising and the school Book Fair.

schedule.text: General membership meetings are held during the 2026 to 2027 school year and are open to everyone. The site does not list meeting dates or times.

cost.text: Meetings are free. Membership is paid each year through the PTA's online shop, and the site does not show the price.

first_step.how: Come to a general membership meeting, which needs no membership. Volunteers who work with students without a teacher present need school clearances first.
first_step.basis: Anyone can attend the general meetings with no membership, and the site gives a clear way to join through its online shop. It describes no newcomer program.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not say how long a general meeting runs or who attends. Minutes and slides from the 2026 to 2027 meetings are posted online. Volunteers help with school events, teacher appreciation, fundraising and the Book Fair.
first_visit_tips: Email president@nebingerpta.org to ask the date, time and place of the next general meeting, because the site does not list them.
If you plan to volunteer alone with students, start the clearances early. The FBI check costs $23.25 and the two state checks are free.
Watch the volunteer orientation, a webinar of about 45 minutes followed by a short quiz, and keep the certificate for your clearance packet.

records.notes: Meeting place and times are not on the site, so the location shown is the school address. The home page mentions a volunteer calendar, but the get-involved page shows no shift sign-up, so the calendar is not confirmed. Clearances, per the clearances page, are needed for volunteers without faculty supervision and for field trip chaperones. background_check is left out because a newcomer's general meeting route does not need one. The Friends of Nebinger group is listed in leads_only.

records.name: PURR (Philadelphia Urgent Rescue and Relief)
records.summary: An all-volunteer cat rescue run on donations. It trims colonies of outdoor cats, takes in sick or unwanted cats, runs a sanctuary, and places cats through adoption and foster homes.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer with cat rescue and trap-neuter-return work, foster a cat, or help at the cat cafe in Bridesburg.

schedule.text: No regular meeting schedule is published. Volunteer and foster sign-up is open year round.

first_step.how: Email contact@purrphilly.com and say whether you want to volunteer, foster, or help at the cat cafe.
first_step.basis: Open to the public. The site invites people to get in touch to volunteer or foster and names an email address and a volunteer Facebook group. It describes no orientation, and its volunteer and foster pages could not be read.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site names cat rescue and trap-neuter-return work, fostering and help at the cat cafe as ways to take part. Volunteering and fostering are unpaid, and the site does not describe shifts or training.
first_visit_tips: Email before you visit, because the site did not show cafe hours or whether there is a visit fee.
Ask about orientation or training for new volunteers, since the site does not describe any.

records.notes: Three deep pages failed to load: the volunteer page, the foster application and the cat cafe page each returned 'Socket is closed' on the first try and again on retry. They are unread, so the cafe address, hours, volunteer steps and orientation are missing. This group used 7 fetches, one over the cap of six, because of the retries. The only year on the site is a 2026 footer, which is not evidence. probably_active is kept because the site is working and shows no dates.

records.name: Real Life CDC
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that helps people get back on their feet after homelessness, incarceration or addiction. It offers life coaching, workshops and help with food, jobs, school and housing.
records.what_you_do: Ask about one-on-one life coaching, leadership and life skills workshops, or help with food, employment, education or housing.

cost.text: The site does not state a cost for its services.

first_step.how: Call 215-792-3298, or send a request through the contact form on reallifecdc.org, and ask which programs are taking people now.
first_step.basis: The way in is a phone call or a form, but the site does not describe how enrollment works or whether there is a waitlist.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site describes its work as hands on and one on one, but it does not describe a first visit, enrollment steps or office hours. Ask on the phone what happens after you reach out.
first_visit_tips: The site lists only a P.O. box and no office, so call rather than go in person.

records.notes: The events calendar for October 2026 is empty, and the life coaching page gives no details beyond a menu entry. The only year on the site is a 2018 footer, which is not evidence. probably_active is kept only because the site is working and shows no dates, so a reviewer may want to confirm it. The site lists no office hours or physical office. This group shares its P.O. box, phone and contact name with Real Life International Ministries, which is a separate EIN and separate service; see that record's notes.

records.name: Real Life International Ministries
records.summary: A faith-based ministry that gives one-on-one help with food, housing, jobs, health, legal questions and addiction, and offers life skills and leadership training.
records.what_you_do: Call, email or use the contact page to describe what you need. The ministry arranges help one on one and offers training for people who want to lead a ministry.

cost.text: The site does not list any fee for services.

first_step.how: Call (215) 792-3298 or use the Contact Us page on rlimnow.org to ask for one-on-one help.
first_step.basis: Help is arranged one on one after you reach out. The site does not describe meetings, worship times or an intake process, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site describes its help as hands on and tailored to each person's needs. It does not describe a first visit, intake steps or meeting places, so ask what happens after you make contact.

records.notes: The about page names Karen Nichols as the founder of this pastor-led ministry and says it serves churches and pastors as well as individuals in crisis. It lists no worship services or meeting places, so kind is kept as congregation from tier 1 only because the ministry is pastor-led; a reviewer may prefer nonprofit. The events page lists no dated events, and its flyer file names carry 2016 and 2018 upload dates. The only year on the home and about pages is a 2018 footer. probably_active is kept because the site is working and shows no dates. The programs page linked from the menu returned 404. The about page's related sites are WorkDatWord and Real Life CDC.

records.name: Redemption Lutheran Church
records.summary: A Lutheran congregation on Bustleton Avenue in the Northeast with Sunday worship in person and online. It mentions monthly service days, a partnership with Fostering Hope and seasonal Bible study, but gives no dates.
records.what_you_do: Come to Sunday worship, watch it online, or ask the office about the monthly service days and seasonal Bible study.

schedule.text: Sunday worship at 10 am, in person and livestreamed. Monthly service days and seasonal Bible study are mentioned, but the site lists no dates for them.

first_step.how: Come to Sunday worship at 10 am at 8001 Bustleton Avenue, or watch the livestream on Facebook or YouTube first.
first_step.basis: The site says all are welcome, lists a weekly worship time and gives an office phone and email. It links to an 'I'm New' section whose contents we could not see, and it describes no newcomer program.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site describes Sunday worship at 10 am, held in person at the corner of Bustleton and Rhawn and also livestreamed. It does not describe what happens after the service, dress, or whether there is a children's program. The church says it has been in the neighborhood for over 90 years.
first_visit_tips: Watch the livestream on Facebook or YouTube first if you want to see a service before you go.
Call the office Tuesday to Thursday, 8 am to 11 am, with questions about dress, children's programs or parking, since the site does not cover them.
Ask the office for the dates of the monthly service days and seasonal Bible study, because the site lists none.

records.notes: The home page re-check confirmed a weekly livestream on Facebook and YouTube. The Facebook link on the church site goes to a nursery school page, not the church, so it is not used as the church's social link; the nursery school is in leads_only. The ministries page lists SAGES, Fostering Hope Philly NE, Monthly Service Projects and Faith Formation, with no days, times or sign-up steps. The 'I'm New' page was not visible. No parking, transit or accessibility details are on the site. The only year is a 2026 footer. probably_active is kept because the site is working and shows no dated news.

records.name: ReGen250
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit with partner programs on clean energy and cleaner factories, a pandemic recovery program for schools and neighborhoods in Pennsylvania, and a heritage garden project for Philadelphia's 250th year.
records.what_you_do: Get updates through the newsletter, or donate. The site mentions part-time volunteers but describes no sign-up step, and it lists no current events.

first_step.how: Sign up for the newsletter on regen250.org, or call 610-504-2245 and ask how to volunteer.
first_step.basis: The site offers a newsletter sign-up and a contact number, but it describes no volunteer or event sign-up.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe in-person events or a volunteer shift. The main ways in are the newsletter sign-up and the office phone line.

records.notes: The three core programs are Mid-Atlantic China Partnership, Keystone COVID Response and First Capital Garden. The past-programs page lists them as core programs and does not say whether they are current. The tier 1 claim of a six-state region is not on any page read today, so the summary no longer repeats it. The future-program page lists nothing. The newest year on the site is 2026, from a July 4, 2026 mention and the footer. The only dated item is a 2024 solicitation PDF, with its date taken from the file name. First Capital Garden (1stcapitalgarden.org) is a project of this group and not a separate lead, so it is not in leads_only.

records.name: Relâche
records.summary: A music ensemble that presents concerts and collaborative projects, and invites singers and players to join some performances.
records.what_you_do: Attend a listed concert, or take part in a public project such as Unsilent Night, which the group says anyone can join. Multi-week collaborative workshops are also listed.

schedule.text: No regular weekly schedule is published. Concerts and projects are listed one at a time.

cost.text: Some concerts are ticketed, and the site shows no prices. Unsilent Night is free and needs no tickets.

access.notes: Unsilent Night involves over 30 minutes of walking, including crossing city streets.

first_step.how: Come to Unsilent Night, the free group walk around Rittenhouse Square (next listed for Friday, Dec 18, 2026 at 6 pm, meeting at the Guard House), or email director@relache.org to ask about performing in a project.
first_step.basis: The Unsilent Night listing says anyone can take part at no cost and with no tickets. The site describes no audition or join process for performers, so the rating stays at 3.
first_step.what_to_expect: Unsilent Night lasts about 45 minutes and is a group performance on foot through the streets around Rittenhouse Square. You play one of four recorded tracks on a phone or another device with speakers, and organizers help you download it before the countdown. Everyone presses play together when the countdown ends.
first_visit_tips: Bring a phone or other device with speakers. The page says a smartphone with external speakers works best.
Plan for over 30 minutes of walking, including crossing city streets.
Get there early enough to download a track before the countdown. The page gives no arrival time.

records.notes: Re | UNITE is on Sunday, Oct 25, 2026 at 4 pm at the Philadelphia Ethical Society, 1906 Rittenhouse Square. It is ticketed through a Ticketleap link, and no price is shown. Re | JOICE is Unsilent Night, Friday, Dec 18, 2026 at 6 pm, free. Re | OPEN is listed for Sunday, June 6, 2027 at 4 pm. Re | ROOT is titled January and February, 2007, but its description says 2027 Wildflower Lab, so its year is unresolved. The musicians page does not explain how to join a project, so the only join step is email. Venues change per concert, so no fixed location is listed. Status moved from probably_active to active because the site lists dated concerts for Oct 2026, Dec 2026 and June 2027.
